articles.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus

Reddit user ShweetsStuff discovered the songs used during a Grand Theft Auto-themed section. They found several audio files with Suno metadata that pointed back to […]

articles.title: Protesters storm Meta offices in India
articles.short_snippet: Members of the opposition Congress party protested outside Meta's offices in Delhi on Friday and appear to have entered the building in a video shared by CNN. Members of the party's youth wing are demanding the company restore accounts of party leaders and warned of more protests to come. The Congress party has criticized Meta […]

articles.title: Analysis: AI chip rivalry shifts toward system-level capabilities as AMD challenges Nvidia's full-stack ecosystem
articles.short_snippet: Amid the wave of controversy and headlines surrounding Jensen Huang, AMD announced on November 16 that it had completed its acquisition of World Labs in an all-stock transaction worth approximately US$8.2 billion.

articles.title: SmartSens bets US$225M on China's 40nm CIS foundry capacity despite mounting losses
articles.short_snippet: Chinese fabless chip designer SmartSens plans to invest CNY1.5 billion (≈ US$225 million) in Wuhan Chuxing Technology, acquiring a 5.588% stake in one of China's few 40nm CMOS image sensor (CIS) foundries. Financed entirely through long-term bank loans, the investment aims to secure high-end CIS production capacity and strengthen domestic supply chain resilience.

articles.title: XPeng's A868 tilt milestone pushes China's flying-car race into long-range aviation
articles.short_snippet: As China's technological ambitions expand further into physical AI and advanced mobility, competition is increasingly moving beyond short-range low-altitude demonstrations toward more complex forms of long-range electric aviation.

articles.title: AI stock rout puts Taiwan's tech supply chain on alert, prompting government scrutiny of capital flows
articles.short_snippet: A sharp sell-off in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index and shares of major global technology companies has wiped billions off the market value of Taiwan's high-tech and AI supply chain companies. Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) stressed in a statement that the long-term outlook for AI infrastructure remains intact, urging continued confidence in the country's industrial development.

articles.title: Trump-Xi talks set human guardrails for military AI
articles.short_snippet: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during a meeting in Shenzhen that AI must not independently make major military decisions, amid growing competition between the two countries over AI technology and advanced chips.

articles.title: Commentary: Cursor's Kimi dilemma turns open-weight AI into next US-China dependency fight
articles.short_snippet: As the US government continues to tighten controls on advanced AI chip exports amid growing concerns over Chinese technological gains, regulatory scrutiny is beginning to move further up the AI value chain toward the software layer where open-weight model development sits.

articles.title: Apple enters silicon photonics race with optical packaging hires for custom chips
articles.short_snippet: Apple has stepped up recruitment for silicon photonics and optical packaging specialists, sparking speculation that the tech giant is accelerating plans to integrate the technology into its next-generation data center chips. As AI-driven data centers face mounting demands for high-speed data transmission and energy efficiency, silicon photonics and optical interconnects are rapidly becoming the se

articles.title: Taiwan premier summons finance, industry leaders as Jensen Huang scandal ripples outward
articles.short_snippet: Taiwan Premier Jung-tai Cho is set to meet representatives of the financial sector and technology, industrial, and business associations at 3 p.m. on November 23, as the government stepped up its response to the scandal surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

articles.title: SK Hynix to gain voting rights in Kioxia under 15% cap
articles.short_snippet: South Korea's SK Hynix is set to become the largest indirect shareholder in Japanese memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings through a bond conversion that will give it voting rights in a major NAND flash rival, subject to a 15% limit.

articles.title: Trinity Fab in talks to use SK Hynix's EUV tools
articles.short_snippet: South Korea's Trinity Fab is in talks with SK Hynix over the possible use of the chipmaker's extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment to test semiconductor materials, including EUV photoresists.

articles.title: Ingentec targets 12 TGV lines by end of 2027 as FAU and GCB initiatives advance
articles.short_snippet: Ingentec is scaling up its through-glass via (TGV) roadmap to target applications in artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and co-packaged optics (CPO). The company is actively driving two core pillars: glass core boards (GCB) and one-piece fiber array units (FAU).

articles.title: China's neoclouds see confidence shaken as financing dries up
articles.short_snippet: The United States has introduced sweeping new artificial intelligence chip export controls designed to prevent Chinese firms from tapping high-end computing power through data centers in Southeast Asia and beyond. This regulatory tightening has slammed the brakes on the once-booming neocloud sector, making bank financing significantly harder to secure.

articles.title: Allis Electric sees growth from AI data centers, semiconductor expansion
articles.short_snippet: Allis Electric reported consolidated revenue of NT$7.994 billion (US$242.39 million) for the first nine months of 2026, up 7.96% year-on-year. Net profit was NT$687.7 million, up 14.27%, while earnings per share reached NT$2.44, the company said.

articles.title: SoftBank, ABB reportedly weigh China spin-off to save robotics deal
articles.short_snippet: SoftBank Group's planned purchase of ABB's robotics business faces uncertainty after Chinese regulators raised concerns that sensitive robotics data could flow to the US. The impasse highlights the cross-border challenges surrounding technology transactions. The companies are weighing restructuring options, including separating the Chinese operations, while seeking to preserve the original deal.

articles.title: Analysis: AMD lands Taalas, targets CUDA with GPU-ASIC inference
articles.short_snippet: As controversy surrounding Nvidia founder Jensen Huang draws global attention, rival AMD announced on November 18 that it had completed its acquisition of Canadian AI inference chip company Taalas. articles.title: Trump holds firm on China AI chip curbs, leaving Nvidia's H200 exports in limbo
articles.short_snippet: US President Donald Trump has reiterated that Washington wants only older-generation chips sold to China, leaving open the possibility of a broader agreement with Beijing while his administration tightens restrictions on Chinese access to advanced artificial intelligence computing.

articles.title: Commentary: China's AI spending race strains cash flow at Tencent, Baidu and Alibaba
articles.short_snippet: "The wave is already upon us." Tencent chairman Pony Ma's recent warning at an internal meeting captures the urgency confronting China's technology giants in the AI era.

articles.title: Taiwan telecom operator reiterates call for spectrum shift in 5G mmWave market, keeps Amazon Leo talks open
articles.short_snippet: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT) is urging the Taiwan government to lead a phased shift of 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) services from the 28GHz band to 26GHz, preserving the 28GHz band for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications. CHT chairman Chih-Cheng Chien reiterated the company's position on November 20 and said it has not ruled out the possibility of working with Amazon Leo, formerly known as Pro

articles.title: China's memory buildout could boost Korean suppliers as local rivals gain ground
articles.short_snippet: China's memory chip expansion could bring new orders to South Korean semiconductor equipment and materials suppliers, even as Chinese manufacturers gain ground in their home market.

articles.title: AI server prices jump up to 45% after contracts signed, putting buyers at suppliers' mercy
articles.short_snippet: AI server suppliers, including Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), Lenovo, and Supermicro, are reportedly demanding price increases of up to 45% on equipment months after contracts were agreed, reflecting mounting pressure from soaring memory costs and tight computing hardware supplies.

articles.title: Lisa Su praises Jensen Huang as AMD targets 80% data-center revenue share
articles.short_snippet: Calls for Jensen Huang to return as Nvidia's leader have surged over the past week, but on November 17, the board firmly rejected his offer to come back. As uncertainty mounts around a future without Huang, customer confidence is wavering, and competitors are preparing to seize the opportunity.

articles.title: South Korea plans 256-satellite LEO network, but domestic rockets fall short of launch requirements
articles.short_snippet: South Korea is considering deploying a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) communications network comprising 256 satellites by 2035. However, its domestic launch vehicles are projected to place only 27 satellites into orbit between 2033 and 2035, highlighting a significant gap between the country's satellite ambitions and its launch capabilities.

articles.title: Trump's threatened tax on overseas data centers clouds US Big Tech's India buildout
articles.short_snippet: US President Donald Trump's threat to impose a "tremendous tax" on American companies that build data centers abroad has put a question mark over the tens of billions of dollars Google, Microsoft, and Amazon have pledged for cloud and AI infrastructure in India, even though the proposal so far comes with no rate, scope, or legal mechanism.

articles.title: Canon secures JAXA funding for SPAD satellite targeting high-resolution day-night Earth observation
articles.short_snippet: Canon has announced that its project to develop an ultra-high-sensitivity satellite equipped with single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) imaging technology has been selected for support under the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's (JAXA) Space Strategy Fund.

articles.title: Why SoftBank weighed a US$1 trillion SK Hynix buyout before backing off
articles.short_snippet: SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son recently approached Wall Street banks about financing a potential US$1 trillion buyout of South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: ASE, SPIL to overtake Amkor in 2027 as server CPUs shift beyond TSMC CoWoS
articles.short_snippet: Global advanced packaging capacity remains in short supply, with TSMC's fully booked CoWoS lines prioritising AI accelerator customers. Server CPU packaging orders are consequently shifting towards outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) providers, including ASE Holdings, SPIL and Amkor, fuelling demand for CoWoS-like packaging technologies.

articles.title: Weekly news roundup: TSMC to comply with new US rules; Musk approaches Korean firms for equipment
articles.short_snippet: This week's coverage highlighted intensifying investment, supply constraints, and geopolitical pressures across the semiconductor industry. articles.title: India revises domestic value rules for six IT hardware products
articles.short_snippet: India has revised its methodology for measuring domestic value addition in six IT hardware products, changing how manufacturers may qualify for public procurement preferences. The framework could influence sourcing and verification for companies serving India's market, while its emphasis on production, research, and intellectual property may shape global supply chains.

articles.title: DIGITIMES Insight: Startups find opening in industrial IoT as focus shifts from connectivity to intelligence
articles.short_snippet: With global IoT connections past 20 billion and most factories already networked, the next phase of the industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) will turn on whether AI can turn plant data into decisions and action. DIGITIMES observes that the shift is redefining the industrial manufacturing value chain and giving startups a way into traditional industrial markets.

articles.title: Time-to-power crunch pushes Taiwan power equipment suppliers up the AI value chain
articles.short_snippet: AI data center construction remains robust despite tighter US regulatory scrutiny and delays to some projects, sustaining long-term demand for power infrastructure.
